qt: to the Commission Afroditi Latinopoulou (PfE) Subject:

The European Parliament is examining hybrid threats, the instrumentalisation of migrants in Ceuta and the protection of external borders. Articles 67 and 77 TFEU provide for a common border policy and surveillance, while Article 4(2) TEU protects the territorial integrity of the Member States. Greece, as an external border of the Union, faces repeated pressures in Evros and the Aegean through irregular migration flows from Türkiye. However, Türkiye continues to be funded as an EU partner in migration management, without effective implementation of readmissions. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission characterise the organised instrumentalisation of migration flows from a non-EU country as a hybrid threat to the security and territorial integrity of a Member State and does it consider that this is happening at the Greek borders?

Will the Commission make the relevant EU funding to Türkiye conditional on a measurable reduction in irregular departures, effective readmissions and respect for the sovereignty and sovereign rights of Greece?

What legislative, financial and operational measures will the Commission take to guard the external borders, border procedures, detention where provided for by EU law and faster returns, instead of transferring the problem between Member States?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) The instrumentalisation of migrants by third countries is a serious security challenge for the EU and its Member States. It puts at risk not only the national security and sovereignty of Member States but also the safety and integrity of the Schengen area and the security of the EU, as a whole. The EU deploys financial, operational and diplomatic efforts, including with countries of origin and transit, when and where necessary. National security is the responsibility of Member States. Türkiye is a candidate country and key partner for the EU on migration. Cooperation in this policy area takes place within the framework of the EU-Turkey statement of 18 March 20161. The Commission will continue to underline the importance of Türkiye fully upholding its international obligations, including respect for the sovereignty and sovereign rights of EU Member States, and of maintaining effective cooperation with the EU and its Member States on migration including the full implementation of the EU-Turkey statement. The Commission supports Member States in implementing the EU acquis on borders, asylum and return. Since 12 June 2026, the Pact on Migration and Asylum2 has reinforced screening, asylum and return procedures at the external borders, and provides a legal framework for situations of crisis and force majeure. Member States have primary responsibility for their sections of the external borders of the EU, while EU funding and operational support, including through the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, support reinforced border management, fair and efficient procedures and effective returns.
